corrections.claim: Only quarters with QDETECT=1 get LIGHTCURVE_Qn/APERTURE_Qn HDUs; psf_avail marks any detection ('1' even when the flag is '2'), so quarter counts from psf_avail over-count usable quarters; use psf_fraction_flag.count('1') for stitched quarters.
corrections.evidence: Downloaded KIC 3459079 (QDETECT '021110000001000010'): Q1 has PSFFRAC=0.014 (flag '2') yet has a LIGHTCURVE_Q1 HDU with 1,624 finite FLUX values and appears in the stitched table with 0 finite FLUX (NaN) - paper l.579 'We still include all the extracted quarters ... regardless of low PSFFRAC'. QDETECT equals psf_fraction_flag exactly in every file checked. Catalogue-wide per-quarter cross-tab: psf_avail=1 & flag=2 in 1,417,775 slots, psf_avail=0 & flag=1 in 358,493 slots, psf_avail=0 & flag=2 in 398,674. psf_avail='1' means the per-quarter PSF FLUX column is populated (Gaia DR3 2102612715913245696: avail=0 quarters have 0 finite per-quarter FLUX but finite SAP and finite stitched FLUX). So psf_fraction_flag.count('1') over-counts usable quarters (25,709 vs 23,157 in the pool); the correct usable count is positions with psf_avail=='1' AND psf_fraction_flag=='1'. For sources with catalogue psffrac>0.5 (the minimum over detected quarters) no '2' can occur (0 of such rows), so Kuber's psf_avail count was adequate for his sample.

additions: The KBonus team itself is running a systematic transit search: Moquin et al., 2026 Sagan Summer Workshop poster 41 (https://vmnexsci.ipac.caltech.edu/workshop/2026/posters/Poster_JulieMoquin_41.pdf) with the TraSHDUMP matched-filter TCE pipeline (MES threshold 7.1 sigma, weak-secondary test), RECYCLEBin flux-level vetting (Robovetter-derived), INCInERATOr pixel-level PRF localisation, kiauhoku/SPOTS stellar parameters, TRICERATOPS-PLUS and AO imaging; first candidate BOI-1.01 (G=17.8 M dwarf, 0.51 Rsun, P=3.37 d, Rp=2.94+/-0.15 Re); they state 'an expected yield of several hundred new planet candidates', 'triple the number of planet-search stars' and 'an increase in the number of M dwarfs by a factor of seven'. Any replication must position itself relative to this (speed, disclosure, differentiation) and check candidates against BOI designations.

Flux-vs-magnitude consistency test (new, catalogue-wide, verified): for Kepler targets with 12<G<16, log10(psf_mean_flux)+0.4*G = 10.11 with 0.03 dex scatter (weakly colour dependent: 10.09 at BP-RP<0.6, 10.13 at 0.9-1.5, 10.06 at >3.0). In the background quality pool 32.8% of sources have PSF flux >2x (0.3 dex) brighter than Gaia G predicts (1.2% at G<14, 7.9% at 14-16, 17% at 16-17, 30% at 17-18, 47% at 18-19). The excess is leakage from the TPF host: too-bright fraction vs contrast G_src-G_host is 0.1% (1-2 mag), 5% (2-3), 24% (3-4), 49% (4-5), 70% (>5 mag), and the median excess is 8% of the host's PSF flux. 801 of Kuber's 1,800 eligible M dwarfs (45%; 14 of his first 64) fail this test; KIC 5689121 passes (0.006 dex). Applying |dex|<=0.3 leaves a clean pool of 15,473 non-target sources (G<17: 5,466; G<16: 2,000), written to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ZyushgPlanet/0a31cad6-114a-5cca-8219-924182316e90/scratchpad/verify-kbonus-dataset/background_pool_fluxconsistent.csv.

Stitched FLUX provenance pitfall: LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED.FLUX is each quarter's PSF flux rescaled to the catalogue psf_mean_flux (so quarter offsets are hidden) and is populated even where the per-quarter PSF FLUX is all NaN (psf_avail='0'); for failed extractions the per-quarter PSF medians can vary 60x between quarters while the stitched series looks flat. Always read LIGHTCURVE_Qn, require psf_avail=='1' for the quarter, check per-quarter median FLUX consistency across quarters (after PSFFRAC) and check ITERNEG (ITERNEG=1 quarters have an empty PSF_FLUX_NOVA column).

Kepler-target definition that reproduces the paper: kic in (keplerstellar distinct kepids [200,038] UNION set of all tpforg values [194,770 TPFs]) -> 200,318 targets / 406,582 background (paper 200,352 / 406,548). keplerstellar alone misses 5,451 observed targets; kic==tpforg alone gives 181,681. 341,081 catalogue rows have a KIC number but were never Kepler targets (KIC is an input catalogue), so 'has a KIC' never means 'was searched'.

Flag semantics established from files: psf_fraction_flag == QDETECT ('0' no HDU, '1' PSFFRAC>0.5 and stitched, '2' PSFFRAC<0.5 with an HDU but NaN in the stitched FLUX); psf_avail = per-quarter PSF FLUX column populated; sap_avail = SAP populated (SAP exists for 757,125 quarter-slots where PSF does not). Usable-quarter count = sum(psf_avail[i]=='1' and psf_fraction_flag[i]=='1'). Catalogue psf_mean_flux is NaN for 156,955 sources (155,632 background) - these have SAP only.

Wang & Esamdin 2025, AJ, DOI 10.3847/1538-3881/ade718 ('The Transit Signal of KOI-1755 Originates from a Background Eclipsing Binary Star - Extracting the Light Curve of a Faint Background Star from Kepler Target Pixel File Data'): pixel-level TPF modelling + centroid shifts + Gaia DR3 cross-match reattributed the 25-d KOI signal to a 6.14-d background EB. Direct precedent for the KOI-false-positive-neighbour pool; 1,889 KOIs are FALSE POSITIVE with koi_fpflag_co=1 (of 4,839 FPs) in cumulative; kois-nns covers 8,073 KOIs with every Gaia source within 30 arcsec.

Module-3 primary sources: Kepler Data Characteristics Handbook KSCI-19040-005 §4.6 ('All 4 outputs of Module 3 failed at 17:52 UTC Jan 9, 2010 during LC CIN 12935'; '20% of the FOV suffered a one-quarter data outage every year'), and Batalha et al. 2013 (arXiv:1202.5852: channels 5-8, 1,022 of 4,397 Q4 cadences, ~19% of targets observed 3 of 4 quarters). Season/channel mapping for KIC 5689121 verified from the per-quarter headers (season 0: mod 11 ch 34; 1: mod 23 ch 78; 2: mod 15 ch 50; 3: mod 3 ch 6, lost).

M-dwarf selection provenance: the 29,800-entry M-star catalogue follows Bentley, Tinney & Sharma 2018 (arXiv:1804.06982, 'The Photometric Selection of M-dwarfs using Gaia, WISE and 2MASS photometry') plus Gaia Teff cuts (paper l.695); it is a photometric candidate list, not a spectroscopic sample (Kuber's audit says the same).

lightkurve estimate_cdpp works on these products (472.9 ppm for the target with 'hardest'); it returns a Quantity in ppm, so never wrap it in float() (gives 4.5e-4). transit_duration=13 cadences = 6.37 h; 12 cadences gives 489.5 ppm.

remaining_uncertainties: What exactly populates LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED.FLUX in quarters where the per-quarter PSF FLUX is all NaN (psf_avail='0'): it is not a scaled copy of SAP_FLUX (correlation 0.02-0.5) and the code path is undocumented; treat those quarters as unusable until psfmachine/KBonus stitching code is read.

Moquin et al. 2026 (TraSHDUMP/BOI-1.01): only the poster PDF was read; the abstract/author QR links and any paper in preparation were not retrieved, the Gaia/KIC identity of BOI-1 is unknown, and no refereed publication was found as of 2026-10-17. Whether their 'several hundred' candidates have been or will be released (and when) is unknown.

Citing-literature enumeration is incomplete: OpenAlex (12) and Semantic Scholar rate-limited after 8 titles; Crossref says 13. An ADS query of 2023AJ....166..265M citations with a token is still the definitive check.

The flux-vs-G consistency test uses the catalogue psf_mean_flux and Gaia G; it will also flag genuinely variable or unresolved-binary sources and sources with bad Gaia G, and its colour correction is calibrated only on Kepler targets (0.03-0.05 dex scatter). Its interpretation as host leakage rests on the strong contrast dependence, not on per-star pixel analysis.

The 28-star CDPP-vs-G table was not independently re-run (numbers taken from the saved per-star CSV); a few hundred stars per bin split by colour/dwarf-giant are still needed for a detection-threshold model.
The SAP depth of KIC 5689116 at Kuber's ephemeris depends on detrending (brief 633+/-221 ppm; this check 13+/-53 ppm); the PDCSAP value (~100 ppm) is robust.
Whether Barber et al. 2022 assigned KIC 5689116's PDCSAP curve to Gaia 2103792461826460288 remains an inference from the ReadMe note and the fact that the source was never a Kepler target.
FLATTEN_MASK bit meaning and the flatten's exact parameters remain undocumented (behaviour-inferred: sigma-clip/outlier mask of a 2-day b-spline flatten).

NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP spatial functions: CONTAINS on cumulative fails with an Oracle 'HTM20' error and on ps hits Cloudflare from this sandbox; whether CONTAINS works on any table from other networks was not tested.
